best_for: Linux and Steam Deck gamers with Epic, GOG or Amazon libraries who want those games in one open-source launcher instead of the official Windows-only clients.
description:
Heroic Games Launcher is an open-source game launcher from the Heroic team, built with Electron, React and TypeScript. Behind the scenes it uses Legendary for Epic games, the team's own gogdl for GOG, and Nile for Amazon. The project takes donations through Patreon, PayPal and Ko-fi.

If a game is already on your drive, you can import it instead of downloading it again, and Heroic can sync with an existing Epic Games Store installation. You can browse the Epic, GOG and Amazon stores from inside the app, line up downloads in a queue, sort your collection into categories you define, and change the look with custom themes.

points.title: Three stores in one window
points.text: Heroic signs in to your existing Epic Games, GOG and Amazon Games accounts, then installs, updates, repairs and moves games from all three. You still need an account at each store you use.

points.title: Built for Linux gaming
points.text: On Linux it runs Windows games through Wine or Proton, can download other Wine and Proton builds, and shows ProtonDB and Steam Deck compatibility. On macOS it uses CrossOver instead. Those runners are not part of the Windows build, where games run natively.

points.title: Cloud saves and outside games
points.text: It syncs saves with the store clouds and lets you add games and apps that came from somewhere else, so they launch from the same library.

points.title: Anti-cheat is game by game
points.text: Online Epic games with anti-cheat may or may not work on Linux and macOS. That depends on each game, not on Heroic.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Heroic is GPL-3.0 software with no paid tier. Support for distributions beyond Ubuntu LTS, Fedora and Arch is community help on Discord, not promised by the project.

points.title: Platform notes
points.text: The README lists Windows 10 and 11 and macOS 14 or newer. Windows gets x64 and Arm64 builds, as per-user or machine-wide installers or a portable .exe. The Linux Flatpak on Flathub is verified as published by the Heroic team.

points.title: Older releases on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 59 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need the project's GitHub releases.
